conceptTag: Does a dating app have network effects?
readerTitle: Millions of members, twelve people nearby: the network inside a dating app
caseNote: 가상 사례 (데이팅 앱 창업, 청소 예약 플랫폼) + 실제 기업 문구 (Hinge의 'designed to be deleted') + 일반적 관찰 (여러 앱 동시 사용)
insight: 데이팅 앱의 네트워크 효과는 전체 가입자 수가 아니라 내 근처의 잘 맞는 사람 수로 생기며, 사람이 늘수록 오히려 나빠지기도 한다.
misconception: 가입자가 많은 데이팅 앱일수록 무조건 더 좋고, 한 번 커지면 따라잡을 수 없다.

sources.text: Hinge, brand campaign and company materials ("designed to be deleted")
앱 장면, 창업 계획, 청소 예약 플랫폼은 설명용 가상 사례

factChecks.note: Hinge가 'designed to be deleted'라는 문구를 공식 마케팅에 쓴 시기와 현재 사용 여부를 게시 전에 Hinge 자료로 확인하세요. 카드에는 연도를 쓰지 않았습니다.
사용자가 여러 데이팅 앱을 동시에 쓰는 경향은 일반적 관찰로만 적었고 수치는 넣지 않았습니다. 수치를 추가하려면 1차 출처가 필요합니다.
훅 카드의 '12 people within 10 miles'는 가상 수치입니다.

cards.title: Millions of members, twelve people nearby
body: Your friend moves to a small town and downloads a dating app. The app store page says *millions of members*.
She sets her distance to 10 miles and her age range to her thirties. Twelve profiles appear. By Thursday she has seen them all.
Millions of members did nothing for her. So does this app have network effects, or not?

image.label: Phone showing a nearly empty map of nearby profiles
image.brief: 스마트폰 화면에 지도가 있고, 반경 원 안에 프로필 점이 몇 개뿐. 화면 위쪽에 큰 글씨로 "Millions of members". 따뜻한 일상 톤의 일러스트. 실제 앱 로고와 UI는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Your investor wants one million users.
body: You're launching a dating app. Your investor says: "Network effects kick in once we pass one million users. Spend whatever it takes to get there."
Which plan do you choose?

options.text: A national ad campaign to hit one million sign-ups fast
options.feedback: You'd hit the headline number, spread thin across hundreds of towns. This ignores **local vs global networks**: each user only feels the people near them.

options.text: Launch city by city, moving on only once each city has plenty of active local members
options.feedback: This treats the app as many small local networks and fills each one before the next. Slower on the headline number, stronger where users actually feel it.

options.text: Launch nationwide but let people match with anyone in the country
options.feedback: The pool looks bigger, but most matches live too far away to meet. A bigger network on paper, not a more useful one.

cards.title: One app, thousands of small networks
body: A dating app's value comes from people you could actually date: nearby, in your age range, looking for what you want.

So the network splits into many small pools, by city, age and intent. A million users spread across a country can mean a dozen in your pool. A rival with fewer users, all in your city, can feel bigger.
This is **local vs global networks**. What matters is how full *your* pool is, not the total.

image.label: One large circle broken into many small city circles
image.brief: 큰 원 하나("1,000,000 users")가 작은 원 여러 개로 쪼개진 인포그래픽. 각 작은 원에 "City · age · looking for" 라벨. 한 원은 꽉 차 있고 다른 원은 거의 비어 있음.

cards.title: Growth is working. Complaints are rising.
body: Your app is now popular in one city. But reviews are turning. Some users say their inbox is flooded with low-effort messages. Others say nobody replies. Fake profiles are creeping in.
What do you do?

options.text: Push more marketing; a bigger pool will fix it
options.feedback: More users can add more of the same noise. This is a case of **when networks get worse**: past a point, extra people crowd the good ones out.

options.text: Add limits: daily like caps, profile checks, clear filters for what people want
options.feedback: You may grow a bit slower, but each new member adds value instead of noise. You're managing quality, not just size.

options.text: Charge everyone a fee to cut the volume
options.feedback: A fee can filter out spammers, but it also drives away good members and shrinks thin local pools. A blunt tool for a targeted problem.

cards.title: Crowding is part of the network
body: In many networks, each new member helps. In dating, a new member can also mean more messages to sort, more competition for the same few profiles, and more bad actors.
Popular profiles get buried in attention. Others get ignored. Both groups start leaving.
That's why many dating apps spend so much effort on limits, verification and matching. They're not just adding people. They're keeping the network worth joining.

cards.title: The best users leave when it works.
body: Hinge built a brand around being *designed to be deleted*. That's honest: a dating app succeeds when two of its users stop using it.
So the network keeps losing its happiest members and must keep refilling. Many people also use several apps at once, so no single app owns them.
The network effect is real, but leaky. It protects a local lead less than the member count suggests.

cards.title: Now it's a booking platform for home cleaners.
body: You run an app that matches homeowners with cleaners in one city. A national rival has ten times more cleaners in total and is entering your city.
How worried should you be?

options.text: Very. Their total size will win
options.feedback: Total size matters less than it looks. Homeowners only care about cleaners who can reach their street this week. That's **local vs global networks** again.

options.text: Compare local depth: cleaners per neighborhood, booking speed, repeat customers
options.feedback: This measures the network customers actually feel. If you're denser and faster where it counts, their national count doesn't help them here.

options.text: Sign up as many cleaners as possible, without checks
options.feedback: You'd win on numbers but risk no-shows and bad cleans. That's **when networks get worse**: weak members make the whole network less trusted.

cards.title: Count the network the customer feels.
body: We used two ideas. **Local vs global networks:** value comes from the nearby, relevant pool, not the total. **When networks get worse:** past a point, more people can mean more noise and less trust.
**Try it today:** pick one customer and count how many people on the other side they could realistically use this week. Is that number growing, and is its quality holding?
